newsitem.title: HUNGARY: French NATO/Russia summit idea "not urgent" - Solana.
newsitem.headline: French NATO/Russia summit idea "not urgent" - Solana.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said on Thursday he did not consider French proposals for a five-nation summit including Russia to discuss a deal with Moscow on NATO enlargement as an urgent issue.

"It's something from what I know that is still at the level of suggestion, nothing more than that," Solana told reporters at Budapest airport on a stopover on his way back to NATO's Brussels headquarters following a 24-hour visit to Turkey.
"I haven't talked to anybody in Brussels -- if I'd considered it that urgent, as you can imagine, I would have talked," he added. "I didn't consider it urgent."

Diplomats in Paris said that under the proposal, leaders of the United States, Russia, France, Germany and Britain would meet in April to establish the broad lines of a deal on future European security that could enable Moscow to accept the enlargement of NATO.
The U.S. State Department has virtually ruled out the idea, which is backed by Germany, saying it had not received any such proposal and did not expect one would be forthcoming.
East European diplomats in Brussels said they were worried the summit idea would undermine Solana's position as NATO's front-man in talks with the Russians.

Solana, strongly backed by the United States and in close contact with the allies, has held one round of talks with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and is due to hold another in Brussels on February 23.
Earlier in the day, Solana held talks in Ankara with Turkish leaders, who linked their approval for adding members to the military alliance with European Union agreement to closer ties with Turkey.
"I think it has been very positive in order to understand the position of Turkey," Solana said of his 24-hour visit in a news conference at Ankara airport before leaving.

Turkey's first Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan had reiterated Ankara's view that NATO expansion was linked to Turkey's relations with the European Union and its defence arm the Western European Union (WEU).
"They are concerned about the adaptation of NATO. In particular in relation to...the role of WEU," said Solana. "I think we will be able to calm that concern."
